title: Bhakti Saints Acharyas Ramanujacharya
definition: Ramanujacharya (1017–1137 CE) was a seminal 11th-century philosopher and theologian who founded the Vishishtadvaita (Qualified Non-dualism) school of Vedanta, bridging the gap between Vedic orthodoxy and the Bhakti movement.
importanceInUpsc: Ramanujacharya is a perennial favorite in UPSC Prelims (Art & Culture/History) due to his role in the Bhakti movement's evolution, his philosophical opposition to Shankara's Advaita, and his influence on later Vaishnava saints.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Bhakti Saints Acharyas Ramanujacharya.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Basic understanding of Vedanta schools (Advaita, Dvaita, Vishishtadvaita)
Overview of the Bhakti movement origins in South India
